name: Church Admin
shortDescription: A WordPress-based church administration plugin with people records, calendars, rotas, sermon podcasting and premium communication, giving and mobile-app features.
suitableContexts: Churches already running and maintaining a WordPress site
Teams that want their church data in their own WordPress database
Smaller churches wanting a flat annual plugin licence rather than a hosted per-contact service

pricing.summary: The supplier publishes a free version with people, calendar and sermon-podcasting tools. Its current site lists $50 per year for churches of up to 50 people and $99 per year for larger churches; confirm currency, VAT, full premium scope and payment terms before purchase.

startingPrice.qualifier: Small Churches plan, up to 50 people, as published by the supplier

tiers.label: Free
tiers.detail: People and family records, calendar and sermon podcasting

tiers.label: Small Churches
tiers.detail: Up to 50 people; supplier describes communications, rotas, giving and Our Church app

tiers.label: Bigger Churches
tiers.detail: Supplier describes the same premium feature family for larger churches

pricing.trialDetails: Supplier advertises a 14-day premium refund; its older pricing post also describes a 28-day Standard trial. Confirm the live evaluation terms before buying.

dataHosting: Church Admin runs inside the church's own WordPress installation and database. The church therefore chooses hosting, data region, backups, WordPress security, plugin updates, access roles and any connected third-party services. This is not a hosted-service data guarantee.
gdprInformation: Supplier says the plugin includes consent and data-removal tools and that the church's data stays in its own database. The supplier's policy makes the church responsible for its own member-data policy. A church remains responsible for its WordPress configuration, retention, roles, backups, security updates and third-party integrations.
coreFeatures: Our Church iOS, Android and Amazon app
integrations: Twilio described in plugin release history
importExport: Supplier states that the data remains in standard MySQL tables in the church's own WordPress database
WordPress plugin release history refers to CSV address-list download
support: Supplier states it normally replies within 24 hours

uk-purchasing.value: Supplier identifies the developer as Andy Moyle, based in King's Lynn, UK, and describes the product as built for UK and EU churches.

contact-band.value: Supplier prices a small-church plan for up to 50 people and a larger-church plan, while describing typical fit as around 30–300 people.

gbp-pricing.value: The product is UK-focused, but its current public plans are priced in USD rather than GBP; confirm payment currency, exchange rate and VAT.

hosting.value: The plugin stores data in the church's own WordPress database; hosting and backup responsibility remains with the church or its host.

gift-aid.value: Supplier describes premium PayPal and Stripe giving forms with Gift Aid reporting for UK churches.

exports.value: Supplier states that data stays in the church's database and refers to CSV address-list exports in its release history.

editorial.assessment: Church Admin is a viable UK-built alternative for a church that already operates WordPress well and wants to keep people data under its own hosting control. Its broad feature set and low annual licence cost are attractive, but the church inherits the operational work normally absorbed by a hosted product: WordPress and plugin patching, backup recovery, permissions, host security and integration management. It should be judged on that full ownership model, not the licence price alone.
bestFor: Small or medium churches with an actively maintained WordPress website
Teams that want church records, calendar and sermons to live in their own database
Churches able to assign clear responsibility for WordPress security and updates
strengths: Free core version and published annual premium pricing
Active WordPress.org release history and a wide church-specific module set
Self-hosted model can give the church direct control of hosting, database and exit
limitations: Public licence prices are in USD; ask for the UK billing route, VAT treatment and renewal cost
The church owns WordPress, hosting, backup, security patching and incident-recovery responsibilities
A WordPress plugin does not by itself establish safe permissions, safeguarding practices or UK GDPR compliance

procurementVerdict.problem: Replacing spreadsheets while retaining ownership of a church's web-hosted data
procurementVerdict.differentiator: Church administration implemented inside the church's own WordPress site rather than a hosted ChMS
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Audit the WordPress host, update process, backup restoration, permissions and integrations before testing a real rota and member-data workflow
